root_cause.text: The USB anchor was allocated with devm_kmalloc using the parent USB device instead of the USB interface, so its lifetime was tied to the device rather than the interface, preventing automatic release on driver unbind and causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the allocation from `devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, ...)` to `devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev, ...)`, and the commit description states that device-managed resources should be tied to the interface lifetime to ensure they are freed on driver unbind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the device used for devm_kmalloc to bind the anchor memory to the USB interface rather than the USB device, preventing potential resource management issues.
intent_record.what: Changed the first argument of devm_kmalloc from &usb_dev->dev to &usb_intf->dev when allocating rt2x00dev->anchor.
intent_record.how: Ties the lifetime of the allocated usb_anchor memory to the USB interface device instead of the USB device, ensuring proper cleanup when the interface is disconnected.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the device used for devm_kmalloc to bind the anchor memory to the USB interface rather than the USB device, preventing potential resource management issues.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by changing the devm_kmalloc device from the USB device to the USB interface, which fixes the lifetime mismatch and prevents the memory leak.

candidates.rationale: The USB anchor is allocated using devm_kmalloc with the parent USB device (&usb_dev->dev) instead of the USB interface device. This ties the memory's lifetime to the device rather than the interface, so it is not automatically freed upon driver unbind, causing a memory leak.
